source: Males and females between 2 and 6 months were used.

claim: Mouse utilization was supervised by the Vanderbilt Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
source: Mice utilization was supervised by the Vanderbilt Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).

claim: Glu-tubulin is a marker of long-lived or stable microtubules.
source: First, MT stability was evaluated utilizing immunostaining for Glu-tubulin (also known as detyrosinated tubulin), a marker of long-lived or stable MTs (Gundersen et al., 1987; Wehland and Weber, 1987; Figure 1A–F, β-cells outlined in yellow).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that Glu-tubulin is a marker of stable MTs and cites supporting literature.

claim: Glu-tubulin content was high in β-cells at basal glucose conditions.
source: Consistent with our previous findings, Glu-tubulin content was high in β-cells at basal glucose conditions, but decreased following a high glucose stimulus (Zhu et al., 2015; Ho et al., 2020; Figure 1G and H).
evidence: The manuscript states this finding and references Figure 1G and H showing the data, with citations to prior work.

claim: Glu-tubulin content decreased following a high glucose stimulus.
source: Consistent with our previous findings, Glu-tubulin content was high in β-cells at basal glucose conditions, but decreased following a high glucose stimulus (Zhu et al., 2015; Ho et al., 2020; Figure 1G and H).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to data in Figure 1G and H and cites prior work.

claim: There was no detectable difference in overall polymerized tubulin content upon glucose stimulus.
source: There was no detectable difference in overall polymerized tubulin content upon glucose stimulus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), likely due to glucose-stimulated nucleation of new MTs (Trogden et al., 2019), which replace destabilized MTs (Zhu et al., 2015; Trogden et al., 2019).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to supplemental figure data and cites prior work explaining the mechanism.

claim: The ratio of Glu-tubulin to tubulin per cell decreased after high glucose stimulation.
source: Accordingly, the ratio of Glu-tubulin to tubulin per cell, which reflects the proportion of stable MTs within the MT network, decreased after high glucose stimulation (Figure 1J and K).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to Figure 1J and K showing the data.

claim: The density of the MT cytoskeleton was heterogeneous within the β-cell population.
source: Interestingly, the density of the MT cytoskeleton was heterogeneous within the β-cell population.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation.

claim: The overall tubulin polymer content was variable in the β-cell population with coefficients of variation of 58.72% in low glucose and 60.42% in high glucose.
source: While not changed by glucose stimulation, the overall tubulin polymer content was variable in the β-cell population as indicated by the intensity distributions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C) and coefficients of variation (58.72% in low glucose and 60.42% in high glucose).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the coefficients of variation with reference to supplemental figure data.

claim: MT stability was highly variable in the β-cell population, as evident from Glu-tubulin staining ranging from barely detectable levels to highlighting essentially the whole MT cytoskeleton.
source: MT stability was also highly variable, as evident from the Glu-tubulin staining, which ranged from barely detectable levels to highlighting essentially the whole MT cytoskeleton (Figure 1A and D, compare cells with red arrows).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the variability with reference to Figure 1A and D.

claim: The degree of variation in Glu-tubulin amongst β-cells was retained after glucose stimulation, with coefficients of variation of 48.56% in low glucose and 63.46% in high glucose.
source: While the amount of Glu-tubulin decreased after glucose stimulation, shifting the histogram of Glu-tubulin intensities per cell to the left (Figure 1H), the degree of variation amongst the β-cells was retained as indicated by the distributions of Glu-tubulin intensity normalized to the mean for each condition (Figure 1I), and by high coefficients of variation (48.56% in low glucose and 63.46% in high glucose).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the coefficients of variation with reference to figure data.

claim: The proportion of stable MTs within the MT network remained variable in high glucose with coefficients of variation of 78.15% in low glucose and 64.39% in high glucose.
source: The proportion of stable MTs within the MT network (Glu-tubulin to tubulin) also remained variable in high glucose (Figure 1K and L; coefficient of variation: 78.15% in low glucose and 64.39% in high glucose).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the coefficients of variation with reference to figure data.

claim: Ice treatment for 30 min is used to directly assess MT stability because only stable MTs remain after this treatment.
source: As a second measure of MT stability in β-cells, we subjected the cells to ice treatment for 30 min. Since MTs are temperature-sensitive and only stable MTs will remain after ice treatment, this well-established assay is used to directly assess MT stability.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the ice treatment assay and its rationale.

claim: In basal glucose conditions, many cells contained MTs stable enough to be retained after ice treatment.
source: In basal glucose conditions, many cells contained MTs stable enough to be retained after ice treatment (Figure 1M and N).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to Figure 1M and N.

claim: Following high glucose stimulation, the amount of cold-stable MTs significantly decreased.
source: Following high glucose stimulation, the amount of cold-stable MTs significantly decreased (Figure 1O,P,Q,R), consistent with our previous findings and data described above (Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data and cites prior work.

claim: Most of the MTs remaining after ice treatment were positive for Glu-tubulin.
source: Most of the remaining MTs were positive for Glu-tubulin, as expected for long-lived stable MTs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D-K).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to supplemental figure data.

claim: The variation in cold-resistant MTs within the β-cell population was high both in low and high glucose.
source: Importantly, the variation in cold-resistant MTs within the β-cell population was high both in low and high glucose (Figure 1S), confirming that MT stability was highly variable in the β-cell population.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to Figure 1S.

claim: Permeabilization of live cells prior to fixation releases all free tubulin, which prevents tubulin polymerization so that dynamic MTs are lost through depolymerization without being replaced, leaving only stable MTs.
source: As a third test of MT stability, we utilized a method where live cells were permeabilized prior to fixation to release all free tubulin, which acutely decreases tubulin concentration in the cell (Khawaja et al., 1988). This prevents tubulin polymerization so that dynamic MTs are lost through depolymerization without being replaced, leaving only stable MTs in a cell (Khawaja et al., 1988).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the method and its mechanism with citation.

claim: MT stability is heterogeneous between different β-cells.
source: These three assays indicated that, similar to insulin secretion, MT stability is heterogeneous between different β-cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly concludes this based on the three assays described.

claim: Some β-cells have highly stable MT networks while neighboring cells can have less stable networks.
source: While some cells have highly stable MT networks, neighboring cells can have less stable networks.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation.

claim: MT stability heterogeneity is more obvious after high glucose stimulation when MT stability is decreased in the entire population but remains highly variable.
source: This phenomenon is even more obvious after high glucose stimulation when MT stability is decreased in the entire population, but remains highly variable.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation.

claim: FluoZin-3 dye becomes fluorescent upon zinc binding and highlights the release of zinc co-packaged with insulin in granules at each exocytic event.
source: To detect single-cell insulin secretion in real time, we used a cell impermeant zinc dye FluoZin-3 that becomes fluorescent upon zinc binding, and at each exocytic event, highlights the release of zinc co-packaged with insulin in granules (Gee et al., 2002; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the FluoZin-3 dye mechanism with citations.

claim: Intact islets were attached to vascular ECM to imitate secretion toward vasculature.
source: Intact islets were attached to a vascular ECM, a condition that imitates secretion toward vasculature (Bonner-Weir, 1988; Low et al., 2014; Gan et al., 2018) and preserves the ability of islets to efficiently respond to glucose stimulus (Patterson et al., 2000; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the experimental setup with citations supporting the rationale.

claim: TIRF microscopy was used to analyze secretion from islet β-cells at the attached islet side.
source: Total internal reflection fluorescent (TIRF) microscopy was used to analyze secretion from islet β-cells at the attached islet side (See Materials and methods, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the microscopy method used.

claim: Individual secretion events appear as flashes of bright fluorescence with intensity over time resembling a Gaussian curve.
source: Individual secretion events appear as flashes of bright fluorescence, the intensity of this fluorescence over time resembles a Gaussian curve with only background signal, then an initially tight circle of signal that dissipates after vesicle exocytosis (Figure 2A and A').
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the appearance of secretion events with reference to figure data.

claim: In control islets treated with high glucose, the number of active cells increased.
source: In control islets treated with high glucose, the number of active cells increased as expected (Figure 2B and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and Figure 2—video 1; Low et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data and cites prior work.

claim: A subset of β-cells (60% of cells) remained inactive even after high glucose stimulation in control islets.
source: However, a subset of β-cells remained inactive even after stimulation (Figure 2E, 60% of cells), resembling the fraction of cells with a high content of stable MTs (59% of cells with >300 average intensity of Glu-tubulin, Figure 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data.

claim: Nocodazole completely eliminates cellular MTs.
source: To assess the role of MTs in the distribution of secretion activity in the β-cell population, we preincubated islets in the presence of either the MT depolymerizing drug nocodazole, which completely eliminates cellular MTs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), or the MT-stabilizing drug taxol (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G), which hyper-stabilizes MT networks in cells, dramatically increasing their Glu-tubulin content (Gundersen et al., 1987; Wehland and Weber, 1987; Townley et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the effect of nocodazole with reference to supplemental figure data.

claim: Taxol hyper-stabilizes MT networks in cells, dramatically increasing their Glu-tubulin content.
source: To assess the role of MTs in the distribution of secretion activity in the β-cell population, we preincubated islets in the presence of either the MT depolymerizing drug nocodazole, which completely eliminates cellular MTs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), or the MT-stabilizing drug taxol (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G), which hyper-stabilizes MT networks in cells, dramatically increasing their Glu-tubulin content (Gundersen et al., 1987; Wehland and Weber, 1987; Townley et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the effect of taxol with reference to supplemental figure data and cites supporting literature.

claim: Nocodazole increased insulin secretion specifically in high glucose-stimulated islets.
source: As we have previously observed (Zhu et al., 2015), nocodazole increased insulin secretion specifically in high glucose-stimulated islets (Figure 2C and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and Figure 2—video 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data and cites prior work.

claim: A larger sub-population of β-cells (66% of cells) was activated by nocodazole, compared to only 42% in control islets.
source: Strikingly, we also observed that a larger sub-population of β-cells (on average, 66% of cells) was activated, compared to only 42% in control islets (Figure 2E, compare Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data.

claim: Taxol blunted insulin secretion in high glucose.
source: Addition of taxol also affected insulin secretion as we have previously observed (Zhu et al., 2015), blunting it in high glucose (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, Figure 2—video 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data and cites prior work.

claim: The percent of secreting cells in taxol was only 27%, similar to the percentage observed in low glucose.
source: The percent of secreting cells in taxol was only 27%, similar to the percentage observed in low glucose (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), where MTs are intrinsically stable (Figure 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data.

claim: Modulation of MT stability can change the insulin secretion activity of β-cells within the population.
source: These results indicate that the modulation of MT stability can change the insulin secretion activity of β-cells within the population.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly concludes this based on the experimental results.

claim: Secretion levels were extremely low in cells with a high content of Glu-tubulin (Glu-tubulin intensity above islet average).
source: As expected, secretion levels were extremely low in cells with a high content of Glu-tubulin (Glu-tubulin intensity above islet average), indicating that cells with overly stable MTs are not capable of secretion (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data.

claim: In cells with Glu-tubulin content below the islet average, secretion levels were highly variable.
source: Interestingly, in cells with Glu-tubulin content below the islet average, secretion levels were highly variable, indicating that in those cells other, non-MT-dependent mechanisms significantly modulate GSIS levels.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and its implication.

claim: High glucose caused an increase in the number of events per cell in both control and nocodazole-treated islets, but not taxol-treated islets.
source: We found that high glucose caused an increase in the number of events per cell in both control and nocodazole-treated islets, but not taxol-treated islets (Figure 2I-J').
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data.

claim: The number of events per cell and the fraction of highly-secreting cells in high glucose were significantly increased by nocodazole as compared to control.
source: Importantly, the number of events per cell and the fraction of highly-secreting cells in high glucose were significantly increased by nocodazole as compared to control, suggesting that MT presence attenuates glucose-stimulated secretion in individual cells (Figure 2I-J').

claim: Under all conditions of high MT stability (low glucose in all conditions and high glucose in taxol), secretion activity is distributed similarly throughout the cell population.
source: Consistent with this result, under all conditions of high MT stability (low glucose in all conditions and high glucose in taxol) secretion activity is distributed similarly throughout the cell population (Figure 2I' and J').
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with reference to figure data.

claim: Insulin secretion capacity on both the cellular and population levels is decreased by MT presence and even more so by MT stability.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that insulin secretion capacity on both the cellular and population levels is decreased by MT presence, and even more so, by MT stability.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly concludes this based on the experimental results.

claim: MTs provide a mechanism that supports β-cell heterogeneity in terms of β-cell activation.
source: Furthermore, in terms of β-cell activation, MTs provide a mechanism that supports β-cell heterogeneity.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion.

claim: Changing MT stability in either direction leads to a more homogenous β-cell population with either most cells secreting (nocodazole, no MTs) or most cells not secreting (taxol, hyper-stabilized MTs).
source: While normally the glucose-stimulated β-cell population is highly heterogeneous, changing MT stability in either direction leads to a more homogenous population with either most cells secreting (nocodazole, no MTs) or most cells not secreting (taxol, hyper-stabilized MTs).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion.

claim: Modulation of MT dynamics decreases but does not completely eliminate variability in β-cell activity.
source: It is also evident that modulation of MT dynamics decreases but does not completely eliminate variability in β-cell activity, which is in agreement with the existence of other, MT-independent, mechanisms of heterogeneity (reviewed in Gutierrez et al., 2017; Pipeleers et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion with citations to reviews.

source: In contrast, the likelihood of observing a cluster of three or more events due to random chance is very low.

source: Our analysis (Figure 3E and F) revealed that the number of cells with secretion clusters was small under conditions with low secretion, including all low-glucose treatments and in high glucose after taxol pre-incubation.

claim: Stable MTs in cells suppress hot spot-associated secretion.
source: Interestingly, our correlative microscopy analyses of Glu-tubulin content in β-cells after secretion (as in Figure 2F and G) demonstrated that islet β-cells with high Glu-tubulin content (above the islet average) almost never had secretion clusters (Figure 3G–J), indicating that stable MTs in cells suppress hot spot-associated secretion.

source: Interestingly, in a vast majority of cells with clustered secretion in control, the number of clusters per cell was restricted to one, while in nocodazole, many cells had additional clusters activated (Figure 4E).
